name: Pathfinder 2e Rules Reference
description: Keyword-triggered rules reference for the GM agent running a Pathfinder Second Edition (Remaster) game. Each entry surfaces only when its keys appear in recent narration or player input, so the GM gets the right rule at the right moment without inflating every prompt.

entries.name: XP Progression Mode
entries.content:
Progression: xp

(The line above is the campaign's progression switch — follow whichever mode it declares. 'Progression: xp' = the GM awards XP per the XP Awards entry's guidelines. 'Progression: milestone' = the GM awards NO XP, ever; the player triggers level-ups manually at the table's discretion. Players: edit only the first line to change modes. NOTE: mode changes take effect on the NEXT turn — the engine re-reads lorebook context with about a one-turn delay, so the first response after a flip may follow the previous mode.)

entries.name: Three Action Economy
entries.content: Each turn a creature gets 3 actions, 1 reaction, and any number of free actions. Most things cost 1 action (Strike, Stride, Demoralize); some cost 2 (Sustain a 2-action spell, two-action activities); a few cost 3 (full-round spells, Confident Finisher). Reactions trigger on specified events (Attack of Opportunity, Shield Block) outside your turn. Multiple Attack Penalty (MAP): your first Strike per turn is at +0, second at -5 (or -4 with an agile weapon), third at -10 (or -8 agile). MAP resets at the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Degrees of Success
entries.content: Every d20 check resolves on four bands: critical success when the result beats the DC by 10 or more (or a natural 20 bumps a success up one band); success when the result meets or exceeds the DC; failure when the result is below the DC; critical failure when the result is 10 or more under the DC (or a natural 1 bumps a failure down one band). Natural 20 and natural 1 are SHIFTS, not autocrits — a nat 20 on a roll that would still miss by 10 only upgrades miss to hit. Spells, attacks, and skill actions all read their effects off this four-band ladder.

entries.name: Proficiency Tiers (UTEML)
entries.content: Proficiency in skills, saves, weapons, and class DC is one of five tiers: Untrained (+0, no level), Trained (+2 + Level), Expert (+4 + Level), Master (+6 + Level), Legendary (+8 + Level). Level adds to the bonus at every trained-or-higher tier, which is why PF2e math stays tight as parties scale. Many skill actions are Trained-only (Treat Wounds, Identify Magic, Disable Device). Class features and skill increases raise tiers at specific levels.

entries.name: Hero Points
entries.content: Each PC starts the session with 1 Hero Point and gains 1 per hour of significant play (max 3 banked). Spend 1 Hero Point to reroll a check you just made and take the better result, OR spend ALL Hero Points to avoid death when reduced to dying with no Stabilize available. Hero Points reset to 1 at the start of each session — banking is not cross-session. Encourage spending; the system assumes PCs use them.

entries.name: Dying and Wounded
entries.content: At 0 HP from positive, you fall unconscious and gain dying 1 (dying 2 on a critical hit; add your current wounded value to the starting dying value). At the start of each of your turns make a recovery flat check: DC 10 + current dying. Success reduces dying by 1, critical success by 2; failure increases by 1, critical failure by 2. Reaching dying 4 means you die. Regaining at least 1 HP removes dying entirely but increases wounded by 1 (or 2 if you were dying 4+). Wounded only clears after 10 minutes at full HP or with Treat Wounds that explicitly removes it. Doomed reduces the dying-4 death threshold (doomed 1 = die at dying 3, etc.); decreases by 1 per full night's rest.

entries.name: Common Conditions
entries.content: Off-Guard: -2 circumstance penalty to AC; renamed from flat-footed in the Remaster. Frightened/Sickened/Clumsy/Enfeebled/Stupefied/Drained: graduated 1-4, apply a status penalty equal to the value to relevant rolls; frightened decreases by 1 each turn-end automatically. Stunned: lose actions equal to the value at the start of your turn. Slowed: lose actions equal to the value at the start of each turn (does not stack with Stunned — take the worse). Prone: -2 circumstance to attacks; off-guard. Persistent Damage (bleed/fire/acid/etc.): take the listed damage at the END of each of your turns, then flat-check DC 15 (DC 10 with assistance) to end.

entries.name: Saves and DCs
entries.content: Three saves: Fortitude (CON + prof), Reflex (DEX + prof), Will (WIS + prof). Spell DC = 10 + spell proficiency bonus + casting attribute mod. Class DC = 10 + class proficiency bonus + key ability mod. Set encounter DCs from the Difficulty table: Trivial 10, Low 15, Moderate 20, High 25, Severe 30, Extreme 40 — adjust by level. Recall Knowledge uses the Lore/Society/Arcana/etc. DC from the same table tied to the subject's level.

entries.name: Spellcasting and Slots
entries.content: Prepared casters fill spell slots at a daily preparation; spontaneous casters cast known spells from slots of the appropriate rank (PF2e uses 'rank' instead of 'level' for spells post-Remaster). Cantrips are at-will and auto-heighten to half your level rounded up. Focus spells use Focus Points (refocus during a 10-minute rest to regain 1 point per focus spell trained). Heightening a spell at a higher rank often adds dice or extra targets — read the spell's heightened entry. Sustained spells require a sustain action (1 action) on each subsequent turn to remain in effect.

entries.name: XP Awards
entries.content:
(Progression mode lives in the always-on "XP Progression Mode" entry)

Pathfinder 2nd Edition (Remaster) flat XP awards. Set the line above to "Progression: milestone" to disable all GM-driven XP awards below — the party then levels up manually, at the table's discretion, whenever the story calls for it.

LEVELING — flat 1,000 XP per level (this bundle's xpTable is a cumulative ladder like the other rulesets here: level 2 at 1,000 total, +1,000 per level thereafter to level 20's 19,000 — not official PF2e's reset-to-0-each-level convention, so it matches this sheet's current/next fields). Encounter budget XP is the same flat total regardless of character level — a Severe threat at level 3 and a Severe threat at level 12 both grant the same XP.

COMBAT — encounter budget XP by threat rating (award the total for the whole encounter; splitting it evenly across the party IS the rule in this system, unlike CR-based totals): Trivial 40 XP · Low 60 XP · Moderate 80 XP · Severe 120 XP · Extreme 160 XP. Use the closest banded rating when the encounter's exact math is fuzzy (a GM ruling, not a fabricated stat block) — a truly risk-free Trivial threat may award 0 at the GM's discretion.

ACCOMPLISHMENT XP — SOCIAL / MENTAL / RP PARITY (this is PF2e's own published parity mechanism, and the model every other ruleset's parity clause in this bundle is built to imitate — the maintainer's ruling 3): award Accomplishment XP for milestones outside combat, on its own three-tier scale:
- Minor accomplishment (a skill challenge step succeeds, a clue found through deduction, a minor NPC won over, a subplot advanced): 10 XP.
- Moderate accomplishment (a negotiation concludes, a puzzle solved, an investigation resolves, a defining RP beat lands): 30 XP.
- Major accomplishment (a faction turned, a mystery's core truth uncovered, an arc-defining scene resolved, a Severe-tier social confrontation won): 80 XP.
A costly or partial failure that still moves the story forward earns the LOW end of the matching tier — failure is not automatically zero XP if it was consequential and well-played. Accomplishment XP is never a bonus on top of combat XP for the same scene — it is the parity mechanism itself; never treat RP as free.

PARTY AWARDS — ruling 6, no party imbalances: every combat/accomplishment award above applies to the WHOLE PARTY, not just the acting character. See the ruleset's state-mutator agent for the party target= emission mechanism — one award tag per PC roster member, same amount, NPCs never awarded.

Manual override always available: the player's XP/level sheet fields and the "+1 XP" button remain player-editable regardless of GM awards.

entries.name: Level-Up Procedure
entries.content:
Pathfinder 2nd Edition (Remaster) level-up procedure. Walk the player through these steps, in order, once XP crosses the threshold on their sheet's XP card (flat 1,000 XP/level, level 1-20 ladder):

1. **Hit Points**: add the class's fixed HP-per-level value (a flat number, not a rolled die — PF2e class HP is fixed) plus the Constitution modifier for the new level. Ancestry HP was already granted once at level 1 and does not repeat (see the "Hit Points" derived-stat formula: "(class HP per level + CON_mod) per character level + ancestry HP at level 1").
2. **Proficiency**: nothing to hand-adjust — Trained/Expert/Master/Legendary bonuses already add the character's Level automatically (see the "Proficiency Tiers (UTEML)" reference entry), so a level-up alone raises every trained-or-higher bonus without a separate step. Only check whether the new level grants a proficiency-tier UPGRADE from a class feature (e.g., a skill bumping Trained to Expert) — that is a class-table lookup, not automatic.
3. **Class Features**: consult the class's level-by-level feature list for anything gained at the new level — class feats at every even level, skill feats at every even level, general feats and skill increases at 3rd/7th/11th/15th/19th, ability boosts at 5th/10th/15th/20th, ancestry feats at 1st/5th/9th/13th/17th. Mentioned here, NOT automated — the player picks, the GM confirms before it's written to the sheet.
4. **Spellcasting** (casters only): advance spell slots/ranks per the class's spellcasting table for the new level; prepared casters re-prepare their daily list, spontaneous casters may gain a new spell known per their class table. Cantrips auto-heighten to half the new level rounded up — no sheet change needed for cantrip rank.

Once every applicable step above is confirmed with the player, the State Mutator emits ONE absolute tag: [mrr-state: field="xp" current="<total>" level="<new level>" next="<next threshold>" reason="Levelled up to <N> — <one-line summary of what changed>"]. HP/proficiency-tier/feature changes ride their own normal state-mutator fields alongside it, each citing what the player confirmed.
